questions.question: What exactly triggers the alarm in the laboratory at the beginning of the story?
answers: A power failure of the computing cluster
A deviation of 4.2 sigma from the baseline model in simulation no. 47
A doctoral student accidentally running the night simulation
Loss of connection with the space telescope
questions.explanation: Tadek's phone shows an alert about unconventional activity and a deviation of 4.2 sigma.

questions.question: What does Kamil single out in the data from the galactic centre that raises doubts about pulsars?
answers: The points form a regular structure, not a random distribution
There are no data points on the map
All the pulsars have the same brightness as the Sun
The simulation shows only interstellar dust without emission
questions.explanation: The neural network detects a pattern — the distribution does not resemble a typical population of neutron stars.

questions.question: What alternative instruction does Tadek give Kamil after the doubts about dark matter?
answers: To delete the data and close the project
To run a simulation of an unknown emission process, giving the AI free rein
To publish the results immediately without review
To hand the research over to the Vienna team
questions.explanation: Tadek asks for an alternative simulation assuming a process they don't yet know.

questions.question: Where do Tadek and Kamil send their paper after gathering the data?
answers: To the journal Physical Review Letters
Only to scientific Twitter
To a local newspaper in Gdynia
Directly to NASA without review
questions.explanation: Tadek decides to send the work to PRL, treating arXiv as a fallback route.

questions.question: What does Tadek place in a footnote of the published paper?
answers: A full list of the lost grants
A dedication to teachers who teach through challenges
A warning about a simulation error
The phone number of the Harvard team
questions.explanation: In the footnote he leaves a personal dedication referring to his father's teaching.
